The Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies (AIAS) is pleased to announce an exclusive fellowship opportunity for a researcher who holds a position at a Swedish research institution. The fellowship is made possible through a collaboration with Riksbankens Jubileumsfond in Sweden.The purpose of the AIAS-RJ fellowship is to strengthen the ties and expand collaborations between the Swedish and Danish research communities.

Why apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

AIAS is a haven for intellectual exploration, hosting excellent researchers eager to develop their work in an interdisciplinary, international and collaborative environment. AIAS nurtures an innovative atmosphere where breakthroughs emerge through transparent, inclusive and reflective discussions, offering a space for engagement and creativity.

The AIAS-RJ fellowship gives the selected fellow the opportunity to concentrate on their own research interests while also being an active member of the AIAS research community and participating in and contributing to seminars and activities beyond their own field of expertise. The fellow must be eager to engage in the interdisciplinary community at AIAS and expand research collaborations with colleagues at Aarhus University.

Who can apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

The call is open to curiosity-driven researchers who:

• are of any nationality who hold a tenured position at a Swedish research institution

• work within the humanities and social sciences

• have a research experience of minimum 4 years after completion of the PhD

A unique interdisciplinary platform at AIAS

AIAS fosters connections, sparks ideas and dissolves boundaries as fellows engage with researchers from different disciplines within the Institute and across departments and research hubs at Aarhus University. Therefore, the call welcomes applications from all research areas and themes.

With a location within the unique campus of Aarhus University, AIAS functions as an interdisciplinary platform that connects researchers across Aarhus University and international scholars. AIAS has fellows who work in thematic groups or in individual fellowships, and hosts events and activities, which AIAS-RJ fellows are welcome to join and contribute to.

AIAS and Aarhus University strive to create a multidisciplinary, inclusive academic environment and to be an inspiring workplace for all by fostering a culture in which the individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The fellowship includes

The AIAS-RJ Fellow is offered:

• a salary based on seniority (employment conditions and wages are regulated through the Danish collective union agreements)

• travel costs to and from Aarhus

• relocation assistance

• a moderate budget for research-related costs

The AIAS-RJ Fellow will have office space at AIAS and can participate in academic training activities, conferences and workshops at AIAS. They will also be affiliated with the relevant research environments at Aarhus University.

How to apply: Application process and deadline

Applications must be submitted online via the system: GrantOne.

In the ‘Guide for Applicants,’ you can find the detailed application requirements and more information on the structure of the application system, the selection criteria and the selection process.

Timeline of the application process

• Opening of call: August 2026.

• Deadline for applications: 24 November 2026 at 12.00 (noon) CET.

• Evaluation and selection period: December 2026 - March 2027.

• Applicants will receive answers: Ultimo March 2027.

• Fellowship begins: 1 September 2027.

About AIAS

As an 'Institute for Advanced Study,' AIAS brings researchers together across disciplines, seniority and nationality. AIAS offers fellowships for excellent researchers from all academic disciplines to pursue cutting-edge research projects for the benefit of society and humankind in optimal research conditions.

The daily encounter with colleagues from diverse research disciplines at AIAS provides fellows with fresh and different insights, methods and perspectives on their own research, leading to new and unexpected research questions and ideas.

Data Governance Specialist

Are you keen to support an organization that's on an exciting data journey? Then come join TDC Brands.

As the Data Governance Specialist, you will be a member of the Data Office, responsible for supporting and developing data governance initiatives across the organization. In this role you will work flexibly between the Data Office and embedded in business units to make data roles work day-to-day: enabling data consumers, assisting Data Domain Owners and Data Stewards.

You will have an important role in supporting data governance by working collaboratively with the business.

Key Responsibilities:

Enable Data Consumers:

• Support adoption of the strategic data platform and the Enterprise Business Glossary (EBG) among data consumers in your business domain, including AI and agentic consumers.

• Help consumers find, understand, and trust governed data so it actually gets used for business insights and automation.

Assist Data Domain Owners:

• Support your Data Domain Owner(s) in maturing the data domain map and semantic models.

• Align with Tech, DPO and Legal as needed when data domain priorities, critical data elements, or AI classifications are being set.

• Flag gaps early — missing owners, unclear sources, unresolved dependencies — so each wave starts on solid ground.

Assist Data Stewards:

• Provide on-demand support to Data Stewards as they assess and authorize changes and stay accountable for data quality at source.

Stakeholder Engagement and Communication:

• Act as the day-to-day point of contact for Data Domain Owners, Data Stewards, Glossary Term Owners and data consumers.

• Escalate issues that need central Data Office, Tech, DPO or Legal involvement.

Bonus

Experience with telecoms, familiarity with data cataloging tools, or an interest in how governed data enables AI and agentic use cases.

Qualifications

As a Data Governance Specialist, we expect you to have sufficient years' experience in data management and data governance. You most likely come from an industry that prioritizes critical and valuable data assets and applies 'just enough' data governance.

Key expectations of the role are having great communication skills, comfort in operating pragmatically ahead of a fully defined policy landscape, and an ability to interact with people across the organization to produce tangible benefits to our data and AI initiatives.

•

•

• 
Build reliable frame pipelines from capture to inference handoff to overlay output.

• 
Optimize for stable FPS, low jitter, and deterministic end-to-end latency.

• 
Implement robust camera lifecycle handling: hot-plug, disconnect/reconnect, error recovery.

• 
Work closely with ML engineers to define frame formats, metadata, and timing contracts.

• 
Build diagnostics: dropped-frame counters, latency telemetry, and health logging.

• 
Support production readiness across different camera models and hardware configurations.

Success in this role means delivering stable, low-latency dual-camera pipelines with reliable recovery mechanisms, robust telemetry, and a well-documented architecture that enables the broader SimTech team to confidently build on the platform.

5+ years in real-time video, machine vision, or camera systems engineering.

Strong C++ (C++17 or newer) - preferably on Windows.

Hands-on with Media Foundation and/or DirectShow capture stacks.

Proven integration experience with industrial camera SDKs (IDS peak / uEye SDK strongly preferred).

Deep understanding of pixel formats, color conversion, timestamps, and buffering.

• 
Solid grasp of USB3 Vision / GenICam concepts and camera controls (exposure, gain, trigger modes).

Experience with multithreaded/parallel pipelines and performance profiling.

• 
Practical OpenCV experience for image handling and overlay operations.

• 
Experience designing fault-tolerant long-running services/applications.

Preferred qualifications: Experience with GStreamer or FFmpeg, GPU acceleration, multi-camera synchronization, inference runtimes, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and GenICam / USB3 Vision standards is considered a plus.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Data & AI Architecture, based in Copenhagen or London, to lead our team of four Data, AI and Solution Architects and serve as the design authority for Pandora’s Data & AI platform. This is a genuine dual role. You’ll set the architectural direction and standards, while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge, review and approve the designs that matter.

Our target architecture is Databricks, including Delta Lake, medallion patterns and Unity Catalog, while Azure Synapse and its conformed enterprise models continue to power a significant part of the estate across supply chain, commerce, manufacturing, corporate technology and omni-channel.

A critical part of the role is leading the transition to Databricks: shaping the target architecture, determining where ownership sits as the platform evolves, and ensuring existing solutions remain coherent and supported throughout the journey.

The role is approximately 60% architecture and 40% people leadership. You’ll lead and develop four architects, but this is not a role where technical accountability is delegated to the team. Both sides of the role are real, and you’ll be expected to lead both.

Scope and authority

• Design authority for Data & Analytics: approves data and AI solution designs, and can require rework, attach conditions to an approval, or withhold approval.

• Chairs the architecture review forum, setting its standards, cadence and quality gates, and deciding what requires review against what is already covered by an approved pattern.

• Resolves conflicting design positions across architects, lead engineers and delivery teams.

• Owns reference architectures, solution patterns, data contracts and architecture decision records — accountable for their adoption, not just their publication.

• Owns the team's roadmap, capacity allocation across workstreams, and budget, including engagement of external consulting resources.

• Translates and enforces the Data & AI architecture strategy set by the Global Director, and informs how it evolves.

Job Responsibilities

Architecture

• Set and enforce the standards for what is built on Databricks as the target architecture, what remains on Synapse for now, and what is retired — and on what evidence.

• Decide how data products are aligned: source-aligned versus domain-aligned versus consumer-aligned, where ownership and stewardship sit, and where a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) serves better than distributed ownership.

• Review technical designs from solution architects and lead engineers against platform standards; give feedback that changes the design, not just documents it.

• Define and evolve reference architectures, solution patterns and data contracts so that quality is built in rather than inspected in.

• Lead design sessions with architects, engineering and business stakeholders on complex or contested problems.

• Oversee transitional architectures through to legacy decommission, maintaining business continuity and closing the parallel run.

AI architecture

• Set and enforce architecture standards for agentic systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation, guardrails and observability.

• Set and enforce architecture standards for ML systems: feature reuse, training and serving topology, model lifecycle, and monitoring for drift.

• Approve AI solution designs with enough depth to arbitrate them on the technical merits, and in line with AI policy and applicable regulation.

Governance and regulation

• Embed privacy-by-design and personal data handling requirements into platform patterns, particularly across commerce and omni-channel.

• Maintain computational governance: data quality frameworks, contracts and lineage as platform capability rather than project effort.

Team leadership

• Line management for four architects: coaching, performance, career development, hiring.

• Establish ways of working — review process, documentation standards, quality gates — and hold the team to them.

• Represent architecture in leadership forums, steering committees and cross-functional planning.

• Keep architects hands-on and embedded with engineering teams; architecture produced at a distance from delivery does not land.

What you will have done by month 12

• A published and adopted standard for what is built on Databricks, with evidence of designs changed by it.

• A clear model for data product alignment and ownership, applied on live work rather than documented in isolation.

• An architecture review forum running to a predictable cadence, with a visible ADR record and a known path for challenging a decision.

• Approved agentic and ML reference patterns in use.

• At least one legacy component fully decommissioned, not just superseded.

• A development plan in place for each of the four architects, and any open roles filled.

Essential experience

• 5+ years designing and delivering production data platform solutions at enterprise scale, hands-on.

• At least 2 years line-managing technical specialists, including performance management, career development and hiring.

• Has held a design approval or architecture governance mandate, including declining designs and making that decision hold.

• Has led a platform migration or a parallel-run estate through to legacy decommission.

• Deep working knowledge of Databricks (Delta Lake, medallion, Unity Catalog) as a target architecture, plus enough Azure Synapse (star schemas, conformed models, dedicated pools) to govern what remains there, and pipeline orchestration with ADF or Databricks Workflows.

• Has designed source-aligned, domain-aligned and consumer-aligned data products, with a clear view of where distributed domain ownership beats a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) and where it does not.

• Has implemented or governed a domain ownership model — data mesh or similar — including the federated governance and stewardship that makes it work.

• Has architected agentic and ML systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation and guardrails; feature and model lifecycle, serving, and monitoring for drift.

• Has set architecture standards that others adopted — solution patterns, reference architectures and architecture decision records.

• Has implemented data quality frameworks, data contracts or computational governance in production.

• Holds an architectural position under delivery pressure, and judges well when to concede.

• Communicates architecture clearly to technical and business audiences, including solution designs, ADRs and data flow diagrams.

• Understanding of retail, manufacturing, finance or supply chain business processes and how data flows through a business.

Desirable

• Familiarity with EU AI Act obligations and enterprise AI governance.

Did we get your attention?

We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s experience & ambitions.Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These therapies are designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage, with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Director, Medical Writing, you will be dedicated to one of our compounds under clinical development, taking ownership of the clinical and regulatory writing that helps move this compound through development. You will turn complex clinical and scientific evidence into clear, accurate documents that regulators can act on - connecting the science, data and development strategy into one coherent story.

This is a hands-on role. You will write, shape and drive documents yourself while bringing physicians, scientists, biostatisticians and regulatory colleagues together around high-quality outputs and demanding timelines.

What You'll Do At Hemab

• Own medical writing for one of our leading compounds, from document strategy and planning through drafting, review and finalization.

• Lead development of clinical documents, including clinical study protocols, clinical study reports, Investigator’s Brochures, and clinical submission documents appropriate to the program’s stage.

• Contribute to clinical content of regulatory and safety documents, such as briefing documents, regulatory responses, and DSURs.

• Translate complex clinical and statistical data into clear, scientifically accurate narratives for regulatory reviewers.

• Partner closely with clinical development, regulatory, biostatistics, safety, and other scientific colleagues to align document content with the program strategy.

• Drive cross-functional document reviews, resolve comments constructively and build alignment without compromising scientific accuracy.

• Apply relevant regulatory requirements and guidance, including ICH E3, ICH E6 and applicable FDA and EMA expectations.

• Build writing plans and practical frameworks that keep interdependent documents moving against development and submission timelines.

• Maintain document quality, consistency and version control while adapting quickly as data, priorities and timelines evolve.

• Identify writing or documentation risks early, take ownership of solutions and give the program team a clear view of what is needed next.

• Collaborate with internal cross-functional teams and external vendors to manage public disclosure activities in compliance with transparency rules.

What You'll Bring to Hemab

Essential:

• Bachelor’s degree or higher in a scientific discipline, with at least 10 years of hands-on medical writing experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical or CRO clinical research environments.

• Significant experience authoring clinical and regulatory documents across drug development.

• Strong working knowledge of ICH E3, ICH E6 and relevant FDA and EMA requirements.

• Scientific fluency and the ability to interpret clinical trial data and statistical outputs accurately.

• Excellent written English, with the ability to make complex science clear, structured and precise.

• Strong cross-functional communication skills and experience bringing multiple expert reviewers to alignment.

• Ability to own competing documents and deadlines independently while maintaining quality.

Nice to have

• Advanced scientific degree such as an MS, PhD or PharmD.

• Medical writing certification or relevant regulatory affairs training.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. You'll create some of the writing frameworks you need rather than inherit a finished system. We work across Copenhagen and Cambridge and priorities can move quickly as clinical data and development plans change.

You'll need to solve problems when you reach the first wall rather than pass them on. That means taking ownership, asking for help when you need it, working without ego and being comfortable making progress when every answer isn't available yet. At a company our size, how you work matters as much as pedigree. Good structure should help people move faster and trust the work, not slow them down.

Why Hemab

Your writing will sit close to the point where clinical science becomes a potential treatment for patients. People living with serious bleeding disorders have spent too long reacting to bleeds after they happen. We're working to give them the chance to prevent them.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty and respect. We want the same from our hiring experience - transparent, human and clear from first conversation to final answer.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. Reasonable adjustments are available at any stage of the hiring experience.

Equal Employment Opportunity

All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Electrical and Computer Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
PhD Position in Physical AI: Adaptive Foundation Models for Robotics

Research area and project description
Applications are invited for a three-year PhD position in Physical AI at Aarhus University's Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. The candidate will join the Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, supervised by Associate Professor Behzad Bozorgtabar and co-supervised by Professor Qi Zhang.

Research vision
How can intelligent robots understand instructions, anticipate the consequences of actions, and adapt reliably when the physical world changes? The project connects multimodal perception, reasoning and action with predictive learning and edge intelligence.

Research directions and objectives

Vision-language-action models (VLAs)
Investigate VLA models and multimodal representations that connect visual observations and language instructions to robot behaviour, including learning from demonstrations and generalisation to unfamiliar tasks, objects or environments.

World models and planning
Develop models that predict how the physical world responds to actions, supporting planning and learning from interaction. Possible directions include learning from video, demonstrations and simulation, and transferring knowledge across robot configurations.

Adaptation and edge intelligence
Develop efficient methods for maintaining reliable behaviour under changing environments, sensing conditions and resource constraints. Topics may include test-time and continual adaptation, uncertainty-aware decision-making, and efficient inference and model updates under latency, memory and energy limits.

The precise research focus will be developed with the successful candidate within these connected directions. Research will emphasise new learning algorithms and rigorous evaluation using public datasets, simulation and, where available, robotic and edge-computing platforms. Evaluation will consider task success, generalisation, reliability and computational efficiency. The goal is original research for leading machine-learning, computer-vision and robotics venues. The successful candidate will be expected to conduct original, high-quality research targeting publications at top-tier machine learning, computer vision and robotics conferences, including NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, CoRL, RSS and ICRA.

Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences:

Essential qualifications
A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent), completed by enrolment, in computer science, electrical or computer engineering, robotics, machine learning or a related field; strong academic results and foundations in machine learning, linear algebra, probability and optimisation; and strong Python and PyTorch (or comparable framework) skills.

Only applicants who demonstrate substantial hands-on experience implementing, training and evaluating deep-learning models will be considered. General interest in AI or experience limited to running tutorials or using pretrained-model APIs is not sufficient.

Applicants must provide evidence of research potential through a substantial thesis, research project, code contribution or publication, clearly identifying their own technical contribution.

Desirable experience
Research experience in multimodal foundation models or robot learning is particularly desirable, especially involving vision–language–action models or world models. Experience in model adaptation or efficient edge deployment is an additional advantage. We particularly value substantial technical contributions, demonstrated through a thesis, research project, code contribution or publication. Prior publications and hands-on robotics experience are advantageous but not required.

Application and selection
Include a one-page statement of interest identifying relevant research directions and your strongest technical project; a CV with a project portfolio and publications, where applicable; and Bachelor's and Master's transcripts and diplomas, as available. Provide links or an accessible description of relevant code, methods and results, and explain your personal contribution.

Shortlisted applicants should be prepared to discuss their own implementation, experimental design, results and limitations in a technical interview. Clear scientific communication in English and a commitment to reproducible research are essential.

Use the project description from this announcement; a separate research proposal is not required.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE), Faculty of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Finlandsgade 22, 8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Behzad Bozorgtabar, behzad@ece.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Qi Zhang, qz@ece.au.dk (co-supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk
How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline 01 November 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 01 January 2027.

• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which everyone has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants. All interested candidates are encouraged to apply, regardless of their personal background. jobs.description:
Applications are invited for one or more fully funded PhD scholarships at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark, Odense.

Depending on academic qualifications, applicants may be enrolled in either the 4+4 or the 5+3 PhD programme. Both programmes include a research stay abroad, typically of six months’ duration, and offer a competitive full-time salary.

We aim to appoint the successful candidate as soon as possible, ideally with a start date of 15 January  2027, while remaining flexible regarding the exact timing.

About the Department and Research Environment

The Department of Economics is an international department with a strong tradition of excellence in research and teaching across a wide range of fields within economics. Research, teaching, and outreach activities are organized within four research groups: Econometrics and Data Science; Economic History; Macroeconomics; and Microeconomics. Further information about the department and its research groups is available on the department website.

The PhD student will be affiliated with the Historical Economics and Development Group (HEDG), which focuses on Economic History with a strong emphasis on applied microeconomics and causal inference. HEDG is internationally acknowledged as a leading research group and attracts substantial grants and media coverage, as well as publishing books and articles with top outlets.

The position

The successful candidate will become part of an international research environment and work closely with Associate Professor Anthony Wray on Private Foundations, a Carlsberg Foundation-funded project on the roles of private investment and medical education in shaping innovation and inequality in the United States during the early twentieth century. For further information about the project, please see this link.

These are applied microeconomic questions in health, labour, education, and demographic economics, approached with historical data. We are interested in strong applied microeconomists broadly, not only in candidates who already identify as economic historians, and there is scope for the PhD student to develop their own questions within the project.

The successful candidate is expected to contribute to high-quality research within the scope of the project, including independent, single-authored work. In addition, the candidate will be involved in teaching and supervision within economics at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

The PhD student will be supervised by Associate Professor Anthony Wray and will join a research group that includes two postdoctoral researchers and scientific research assistants, with access to an international network of collaborators.

The project has its own GPU environment — university hardware, reserved for this project and its research team. It runs open-weight models locally for large-scale digitisation and data extraction from historical sources, alongside frontier models. We are also building an autonomous workflow for agentic-supported academic research, and the PhD student will have the chance to help develop that workflow.

Applicants’ profile

Applicants should have completed a relevant master’s degree in Economics, Mathematics and Economics, or related disciplines. Qualified candidates currently enrolled in a relevant master’s programme are also welcome to apply. Furthermore, we expect applicants to:

• 
Have solid knowledge of econometrics and applied quantitative methods, with experience using Python, R, Stata, or similar tools, and be eager to learn and apply new methods.

• 
Be dedicated, capable of working independently and in cooperation with a PhD supervisor.

• 
Have strong English skills, both spoken and written. 

• 
Have good interpersonal skills, be interested in engaging with national and international researchers.

The following qualifications are an advantage

• 
Have an interest in, or potentially experience with, machine learning, large language models, and natural language processing.

• 
Experience working with large datasets and conducting empirical research. 

• 
Demonstrated interest in economic history or cultural economics.

We are an international department, and the working language is English.

Further information about the position can be obtained from Head of Administration Astrid Holm Nielsen, e-mail: astni@sam.sdu.dk. For general questions regarding relocation, housing, taxes etc., contact the SDU’s International Staff Office. 

How to apply for this position

Employment as a paid PhD fellow takes place in accordance with the circular of 20 December 2021 on the collective agreement for academics in the state – appendix 5, protocol on PhD fellowships.

For more information on the department guidelines for qualification and recruitment please see our Appointment Guidelines.

The application must include (all attachments must be in Adobe PDF format): 

• 
Detailed CV - the education and work history must be month and year specific.

• 
A certified copy of your master’s degree certificate, including transcripts of all examination results. Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used. If your degree has not yet been completed, please state your expected date of completion.

• 
A motivational letter describing why you are a good match for analyzing the topic and how your skills provide a solid foundation to do so (max. 5 pages incl. reference list).

• 
A project description (max 5 pages of 2400 characters each, including spaces, notes, appendices, bibliography etc.).

When applying for a PhD scholarship, please fill in the application form available on our web page. 

On the webpage of the PhD-school, you can find the guidelines for preparing your project proposal.

All non-Danish documents must be translated into English. 

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material.

Once the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the portion of the evaluation that pertains to them.

Applications that are incomplete regarding the above requirements will not be assessed by the committee.

Shortlisting and tests may be used in the assessment process.

As part of the overall assessment of the applicant’s qualifications, an interview may be applied.

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

The application and CV must not exceed 10 MB.

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, 23.59 CET/CEST.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website. Uploaded files must be in Adobe PDF (unlocked) or Word format.

We recommend that you read the guideline for applicants. If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk before the application deadline.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

Salary and employment terms
Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

The Department of Accounting invites applications for a PhD position in Auditing. The Department of Accounting is one of the oldest and largest accounting departments in Europe. We have a growing and flourishing research environment within financial accounting, management accounting and control, auditing, and corporate governance.

We especially welcome PhD proposals that adopt qualitative research methods and suggest novel approaches to the study of

• The making of the audit profession, especially regarding emerging technologies in auditing, such as generative artificial intelligence, with an emphasis on how they may reshape the audit profession, including the training and socialization of auditors, the exercise of professional judgment and the relevance of the traditional audit model in responding to evolving societal demands.
• Audit firm ownership, including the emerging role of private equity firms acquiring ownership interests in audit firms. Proposals within this research theme may explore implications for, for example, the partnership model, audit firm governance, how audits are conducted, talent management, client portfolios, audit market competition, and how these developments may reconfigure the audit profession.
• The role of auditing and assurance in sustainable development. Within this theme, candidates are encouraged to explore alternative forms of auditing and assurance that contribute to sustainable development and to propose empirical work that goes beyond simply examining the current compliance-oriented role associated with the verification of sustainability reports. Proposals should aim to develop research that provides a basis for debate about how auditing and assurance can play a meaningful role in sustainability.
• Regulator-auditor interaction, with a focus on challenges and potential pathways in public oversight practices, including, for example, the role of firm-level oversight practices and dialogue, as well as the role of ad hoc regulatory investigations alongside routine quality inspections.
• Client-auditor interaction, with a focus on, for example, the governance role of audit committees, the negotiation of accounting issues, professional and commercial conflicts, or the role of client technology adoption in the performance of audits.
• Auditing in the context of audit firm organization and governance, with the aim of understanding how increasingly intensive and sophisticated audit firm-level systems (e.g., quality management, incentive systems, performance measurement, and culture/tone at the top) operate to manage and control auditor behavior within audit firms. Within this theme, candidates are encouraged to propose research that can inform reflections on how bureaucracy in audit firms can be balanced, how tendencies toward defensive behavior might be reversed, and how professional judgment at all levels, from junior auditors to partners, might be encouraged.
The project should speak to contemporary concerns in auditing and aim to contribute to academic, public, professional, and company-level debates. The PhD project should therefore be informed and enriched by engagement with firms and professionals as part of both the research process and the dissemination of research findings, and we encourage proposals to demonstrate the potential for such engagement.

The PhD position is based in the Department of Accounting, and the candidate will be part of the department’s auditing research group. We welcome applicants with degrees or experience in accounting and auditing. We also welcome applicants from other social sciences who are interested in engaging with auditing as a research domain. The auditing research group consists of researchers with backgrounds in accounting and auditing, as well as researchers from other academic fields who have a strong interest in auditing. The PhD candidate will work in close collaboration with the supervisors and benefit from the international research environment in the Department of Accounting and at CBS. Candidates are encouraged to contact Professor Thomas Riise Johansen (trj.acc@cbs.dk) for informal discussions and information about the position before submitting the application.

About the PhD programme
The three-year PhD programme at CBS gives you the opportunity to conduct research under the supervision of CBS’s associate professors and professors, supported by research related PhD courses. The programme is highly international, and you are expected to participate in international research conferences and to spend time at another research institution as a visiting PhD student. See the CBS homepage for more information about the PhD programme, https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme. 

CBS PhD graduates are held in high esteem not only in academia and research institutions but also in government and business where their research qualifications are in high demand.

CBS is committed to ensuring excellence, transformative and relevant teaching and research. Candidates who wish to join us must be interested in working in an organisation of this type and it is expected that the applicant will show an interest in joining the department's research environment. You can read more about the department's research here: www.cbs.dk/acc

Application and admission requirements
The department will give priority to applicants with high grades from their universities. To be considered the applicant must:

• have a basic education at master's level (corresponding to the 3 + 2 Bologna process)
• have received the grade of 10 (or equivalent) for the master's thesis according to the Danish 7-point grading scale (https://ufm.dk/en/education/the-danish-education-system/grading-system)
• have a weighted grade point average of at least 8.2 on the Danish 7-point grading scale for the bachelor's and master's degree combined or alternatively a weighted grade point average must be at least 9.5 for the master's degree alone. If the grade point average is not met, documentation for being in the top 40% of the class is also accepted. In rare cases, the grade requirement can be waived.
• have completed the master's programme before starting the PhD programme at CBS
• master academic English at a high level in writing and speaking
The application (see link below) must include a five-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed empirical material
• a work plan for the three years
More information can be found here: https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmemes/admission

In addition to the project description, copies of the following must be included:

• diploma for bachelor's and master's degree or other certificates at an equivalent level as well as the grade transcripts
• documentation for being in the top 40% of the class (if grade requirements are not met)
• a concise curriculum vitae (CV)
• a list of articles and publications (if applicable)
• one example of a selected written work (e.g. master's thesis)
The PhD student is enrolled in the CBS PhD School. Further information about PhD scholarships and the PhD programme can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme.Information about the department can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/forskning/institutter-centre/institut-regnskab.

For additional information regarding the PhD position, feel free to contact Professor, Thomas Riise Johansen, trj.acc@cbs.dk.

Employment and salary
A PhD scholarship runs for a period of three years and includes teaching obligations corresponding to 416 work hours. The scholarships are fully salaried positions, according to the national Danish collective agreement. The monthly salary is currently approximately DKK 30,264 up to DKK 36,877 depending on seniority and a pension contribution totaling 18.07%. The scholarship includes tuition fees, office space, course and travel costs (according to the current CBS agreement). 

Salary level and employment take place in accordance with the Ministry of Finance's agreement with the Academics' Central Organization.
